The trial court convicted the appellant and sentenced him to 10 years imprisonment and fine for an offence punishable under Section 449 of the IPC, imprisonment for 7 years and fine for an offence punishable under Section 397 of the IPC and for life for an offence punishable under Section 302 of the IPC.

neutral_facts.value: The accused, along with another individual, entered the house of a victim and committed robbery. During the robbery, the accused dragged a frail elderly woman from her cot, beat her on the head with a wall clock, and robbed her of her jewelry. The victim succumbed to her injuries in the hospital several days after the incident. The prosecution presented evidence including eyewitness accounts, medical reports, and recovered stolen items. The accused was identified by the victim's daughter, who was a witness to the incident. The trial court convicted the accused of murder, robbery, and causing grievous hurt. The High Court upheld the conviction for murder and robbery but acquitted the accused for house trespass with intent to commit murder.

prosecution_argument.value: The prosecution argued that the accused dragged down a frail old lady of 90 years from her cot and caused injuries on her head with a wall clock, which resulted in her death. They also contended that the accused had gone to the house for the purpose of committing robbery and not to kill anyone.

quotes.text: The prosecution case was that while 'JJ' stood guard near the house, the appellant entered the house of PW-1, caught hold of his 11 year old daughter (PW-2), threatened to kill her and robbed her of her jewellery.

defence_argument.value: The defence argued that the absence of a Test Identification Parade (TIP) made the evidence of the victim unreliable. They also contended that the accused had no intention to murder the deceased and, therefore, his conviction for an offence punishable under Section 302 was improper.

quotes.text: In the instant appeal, it was contended for the appellant that since a TIP was not conducted, the evidence of PW-2 could not be relied upon; that the evidence of PW-2, as a child witness should be carefully scrutinized; and that the appellant had no intention to murder the deceased and, therefore, his conviction for an offence punishable u/s 302 was improper.

defence_argument.note: no quote occurs in the judgment; closest passage (p.3, match 93): "and that the appellant had no intention to murder the deceased and, therefore, his conviction for an offence punishable u/s 302 was improper."

legal_principle_applied.value: The Supreme Court applied the principle that the failure to hold a TIP is not fatal to the prosecution's case, but the trial judge must be circumspect in accepting the identification of an accused by a witness in court if the accused is a stranger to the witness. The court also emphasized the importance of victimology and the treatment of victims in the administration of justice.

quotes.text: The sum and substance of the various decisions is that the failure to hold a TIP is not fatal to the case of the prosecution, but the trial judge will need to be circumspect in accepting the identification of an accused by a witness in court if the accused is a stranger to the witness.

sentencing_rationale.value: The final sentence was imposed because the accused was found guilty of murder and robbery with the intent to cause death, but not for house trespass with the intent to commit an offence punishable with death.

quotes.text: On the facts of the case, both the trial court and the High Court were right in convicting the appellant of offences punishable u/ss 397 and 302 IPC. However, as no case has been made out for convicting him of an offence punishable u/s 449 IPC, he is acquitted of the said charge.
